tasks.title: ngv2/grounding.py — semgrep-shaped report -> Finding adapter (impl-only)
acceptance_criteria: NEW file ngv2/grounding.py exists and imports `Finding, SEVERITIES` from ngv2.contracts (does not redefine them).
normalize_severity(raw) is case-insensitive: CRITICAL->'critical', ERROR->'high', WARNING->'medium', INFO->'low'.
normalize_severity returns 'low' for any unknown/unmapped/None-ish input, and the return value is always a member of SEVERITIES.
parse_semgrep reads report.get('results', []) and returns [] when results is empty or missing.
For each result at 0-based index i a Finding is built with id=f"{check_id}-{i}" and target=target.

category is the first CWE in result['extra']['metadata']['cwe'] when that list is present and non-empty, else result['check_id']; missing metadata/cwe falls back to check_id without raising (defensive .get access).
Module is pure/deterministic/stdlib-only: no subprocess, network, file/socket I/O, eval/exec/__import__, globals, or randomness; no public symbols beyond normalize_severity and parse_semgrep.
The committed oracle passes: `python -m pytest tests/test_grounding.py -q`.

spec.objective: Create the NEW file ngv2/grounding.py: a pure, deterministic, stdlib-only adapter that normalizes a semgrep-shaped static-analysis JSON report (passed in as a dict; no tool invoked) into ngv2.contracts.Finding objects, exposing exactly normalize_severity and parse_semgrep, verified by the already-committed oracle tests/test_grounding.py.
functional_requirements: Define module ngv2/grounding.py that imports `Finding, SEVERITIES` from ngv2.contracts and exposes no public symbols other than normalize_severity and parse_semgrep.
normalize_severity(raw: str) -> str maps case-insensitively CRITICAL->'critical', ERROR->'high', WARNING->'medium', INFO->'low'.
normalize_severity returns the safe default 'low' for any unknown or unmapped input, and its return value is ALWAYS a member of SEVERITIES.
parse_semgrep(report: dict, target: str) -> list[Finding] reads report.get('results', []) and returns [] for an empty or missing results list.
For each result at 0-based index i, build a Finding with id=f"{result['check_id']}-{i}" and target=target.

Compute category as the first CWE in result['extra']['metadata']['cwe'] if that list is present and non-empty, else result['check_id']; access defensively via .get so missing metadata/cwe falls back to check_id (a non-empty str) without raising.
Ensure every returned Finding satisfies Finding.validate(), and keep the module pure/deterministic/stdlib-only with no I/O, subprocess, network, eval/exec/__import__, globals, or randomness.
spec.interfaces: from ngv2.contracts import Finding, SEVERITIES; normalize_severity(raw: str) -> str; parse_semgrep(report: dict, target: str) -> list[Finding]
edge_cases: severity strings in mixed/lower case (e.g. 'error', 'Warning') still map correctly (case-insensitive).
result['extra'] has no 'metadata' key, or metadata has no 'cwe', or cwe is an empty list -> category falls back to result['check_id'] without raising.
cwe list present and non-empty -> category is the first element.
Multiple results -> ids are suffixed by their 0-based index preserving input order.
non_goals: Do NOT author, create, or modify any test file; tests/test_grounding.py is already committed.
Do NOT invoke any static-analysis tool, run a subprocess, open a socket, touch the network, or perform any file/I-O access.
Do NOT use eval, exec, or __import__; no globals or randomness; stdlib only.
Do NOT redefine Finding or SEVERITIES — import them from ngv2.contracts.
Do NOT add fields, public functions, or symbols beyond normalize_severity and parse_semgrep, and do NOT change their names, signatures, or return shapes.
Do NOT depend on or import any other Epic-2 child module (poc_runner, report, pipeline).
spec.implementation_notes: Implement normalize_severity with a small lowercase->canonical dict keyed on raw.lower() (e.g. {'critical':'critical','error':'high','warning':'medium','info':'low'}) and a .get(..., 'low') fallback that always yields a SEVERITIES member; guard non-str input by coercing via str() before .lower() if helpful. In parse_semgrep iterate enumerate(report.get('results', [])); compute category via cwe = result.get('extra', {}).get('metadata', {}).get('cwe') or [] then category = cwe[0] if cwe else result['check_id']. Build evidence as a single-element list with the path:start-end string. Construct each Finding via the public constructor and rely on Finding.validate() semantics from ngv2.contracts. Keep the module side-effect-free and import-light (only ngv2.contracts plus optional typing).

test_spec.test_data_requirements: Verification uses the already-committed oracle tests/test_grounding.py (no new test files). The oracle supplies semgrep-shaped report dicts: results with check_id, path, start.line, end.line, extra.severity, extra.message, and optional extra.metadata.cwe lists; plus empty/missing-results cases and varied-case severity strings. No fixtures, network, or filesystem access required.

token_budget_ratio.note: IMPL-ONLY: tests/test_grounding.py is pre-committed, so no test-authoring tokens are spent by this plan. The test_tokens figure reflects the committed oracle's verification surface (>= 1.5x the implementation effort), satisfying the ratio constraint while no new tests are written.
